Interface VirtualServer

All Superinterfaces:
AutoCloseable
All Known Implementing Classes:
VirtualServerTCP
public interface VirtualServer extends AutoCloseable
Client-side abstraction for the server-to-client communication path.

In the client architecture, ServerProxy and VirtualServer represent the two opposite directions of the network connection:

  • ServerProxy: client-to-server path, used by controllers to send user commands;
  • VirtualServer: server-to-client path, used to receive server messages and forward them to the local client view.

The name "VirtualServer" means that, from the client point of view, this object behaves like a local endpoint representing the real server. It does not contain game logic. Its responsibility is to receive messages from the transport layer, translate transport-specific events when needed, and route the resulting server messages toward the UI.

In the TCP transport, VirtualServerTCP implements this interface and runs in a background thread that continuously reads JSON messages from the socket. In the RMI transport, VirtualServerRMI plays the same architectural role through remote callbacks exposed to the server.

Implementations must keep this class of objects focused on networking and message dispatching. User commands belong to ServerProxy; rendering and user interaction belong to ClientView.

  • Method Details

    • handleMessage

      void handleMessage(ServerMessage message)
      Handles one server-to-client application message.

      Typical messages include lobby updates, lobby lists, game updates, and server-side errors. The implementation should route the message to the client-side view layer, usually through the shared client message router.

      Parameters:
      message - message received from the server

    • handlePing

      void handlePing()
      Handles a server keep-alive PING.

      The expected behavior is to ask the matching ServerProxy to send a PONG back through the client-to-server channel. This keeps the heartbeat protocol out of the UI and inside the networking layer.

    • close

      void close() throws IOException
      Releases the transport resources owned by this receiver.

      TCP implementations close the socket-side receiving path. RMI implementations unexport the callback object when it was exported. The exact resource depends on the transport, but callers can use this method as the common lifecycle operation for shutting down the receiver.

      Specified by:
      close in interface AutoCloseable
      Throws:
      IOException - if the underlying transport resource cannot be closed
